correctness.rationale: Atomic restriction of weakly-null Lp sequences tends coordinatewise to zero and the fixed atomic vector has asymptotic norm-power splitting. The sharp Hanner two-sign inequality on diffuse Lp, together with monotone (u^p-A_p(d,u)), forces the lower bound; independent 30,000 random derivative-integrated inequality tests found no counterexample. Nonatomic weighted Rademacher sign sequences converge weakly and attain the p<2 branch; for p>=2 Clarkson gives the lower bound and disjoint finite-measure indicators attain it. Includes t=0, p=2, pure-atomic base vectors; no norm-convergent finite-dimensional substitutes are presumed.

Rodríguez–Rueda Zoca 2023 full text supplies a Rademacher weak-null construction for nonatomic L1 only. Hanner/Clarkson classical inequalities bound arbitrary finite pairs but do not entail weak-null placement and sharp mixed atomic/diffuse attainment without additional measure-theoretic argument. The claim remains a best-of-knowledge profile distinction, with possible older pointwise asymptotic moduli as residual risk.
